prompt.context: You've been called into the headquarters of Galloway Entertainment, a small television production company in New York. The company carefully managed employee interactions during the pandemic, and as a result was able to get through without making significant operational changes. However, the CEO has been reading up on the new 'hybrid work model' and is excited by the opportunity to consolidate her real estate footprint and generate what she expects will be significant near-term operational efficiencies. Her team has pulled together an initial estimate of what it will take to enable a hybrid workplace, and she has asked you to evaluate whether she should pull the trigger.
prompt.question: Should Galloway Entertainment move to a hybrid work model and consolidate its real estate footprint? Evaluate the proposal the team has put together.

clarifying_info.q: What is a hybrid work model?
clarifying_info.a: A hybrid work model describes an environment in which employees spend some, but not all, of their time in the office.

clarifying_info.q: What does Galloway Entertainment do and how does it make money?
clarifying_info.a: Galloway produces scripted television and is exploring getting into documentary filmmaking. It makes money by licensing content to cable television companies and online streaming platforms.

clarifying_info.q: Where does Galloway operate and film?
clarifying_info.a: Galloway films in multiple locations across the US. Operations are currently in New York City, in an office a few blocks away from the CEO's apartment.

clarifying_info.q: What is the CEO's decision-making criteria or timeline?
clarifying_info.a: The CEO's primary focus is making decisions that are cash-neutral or better over a two-year timeframe.

clarifying_info.q: What is the current lease situation?
clarifying_info.a: The company's lease is up in three years. If they want to move, they need to break the lease.

clarifying_info.q: What is the lease breakage cost?
clarifying_info.a: The lease breakage cost is 50% of the remaining lease value.

exhibits.title: Current Operational & Employee Footprint
exhibits.shows: A table of space utilization by employee type (Field Crew, Production, Post-Production, Administration) showing number of employees, current office utilization %, and estimated future utilization % under a hybrid model. Also shows current lease details by space type (Communal Areas & Conference Rooms, Office and Desk Space, Server Room) with square footage, and notes the lease cost is $8.33 per square foot per month. A map indicating area of operations is also shown.

exhibits.title: Proposed New Lease
exhibits.shows: A table showing square footage by space type for the proposed new lease (Communal Areas & Conference Rooms and Office and Desk Space only — no server room listed), plus proposed lease details including monthly rental cost per square foot and a description of the space.

exhibits.title: Hybrid Work Trends & Filmmaking Hubs
exhibits.shows: Two data visualizations: (1) A map of filmmaking hubs with bubble sizes indicating volume of film production students by geography; (2) A bar chart showing expected days in office per week by age group (Age 20-30, 30-40, 40+) comparing Pre-COVID and Post-COVID expectations.

framework: Understand the current operational footprint: space types, square footage, number of effective employees in office, and current annual lease cost
Quantify the impact of the hybrid model on space requirements: recalculate effective employees in office and resulting sq ft needed per space type
Evaluate the proposed new lease: calculate new annual lease cost and annual savings vs. current
Identify missing requirements (server room) and resolve additional costs (offsite server location in NJ)
Brainstorm one-time transition costs and ongoing incremental costs (moving costs, lease breakage, technology)
Calculate net annual savings and two-year cumulative savings vs. one-time costs to assess CEO's two-year breakeven criterion
Interpret market trend data (Exhibit 3) for qualitative strategic benefits
Deliver a recommendation that addresses both the financial result and the qualitative upside, and directly responds to the CEO's near-term savings expectation

questions.prompt: Question 1: How does shifting to a hybrid work model impact Galloway's current operational footprint and space utilization? What does this tell you?
questions.guidance: Candidate should first calculate current annual lease cost, then calculate effective employees in office under the hybrid model by employee type, then derive the reduction in space required. Strong candidates note that server room size is fixed regardless of employee utilization. They should identify the total effective employees drop from 50 to 30 (a 40% reduction) and begin to reason about how much space can be reduced.

math.setup: Current lease: 16,000 sqft x $8.33/sqft/month x 12 months. Effective employees: apply future utilization % to headcount per type.
steps: Effective employees in office — Current: Field Crew 0, Production 20, Post-Prod 20, Admin 10 = 50 total
Effective employees in office — Future: Field Crew 0, Production 20x70%=14, Post-Prod 20x55%=11, Admin 10x50%=5 = 30 total
Current sqft per effective employee: Communal 5000/50=100, Office/Desk 10000/50=200
Note: Server Room sqft is fixed (volume driven, not headcount driven)
math.answer: Current annual lease cost = $1,600,000. Effective employees drop from 50 to 30 (-40%). Communal and desk space can be reduced proportionally, but the server room cannot.

questions.prompt: Question 2: The real estate team found a new space. Under the new lease, how much can they save on an annual basis?
questions.guidance: Candidate should calculate the new NYC lease cost (10,000 sqft at $6.67/sqft/month). Strong candidates note there is no server room in the new lease and ask how the server room will be handled. When told about the NJ offsite (1,000 sqft at $5/sqft/month), they should add that cost. Annual savings = $1,600,000 - $860,000 = $740,000. Excellent candidates note that sqft per effective employee increases in the new space (from 300 to 333 sqft/employee) and question whether the space truly meets needs.

math.setup: New NYC lease = 10,000 sqft x $6.67/sqft/month x 12. NJ server room = 1,000 sqft x $5/sqft/month x 12. Total future cost = NYC + NJ. Annual savings = current - total future.
steps: New NYC lease annual cost = 10,000 x $6.67 x 12 = $800,000
NJ server room annual cost = 1,000 x $5 x 12 = $60,000
Effective cost per sqft blended future = $860,000 / 11,000 sqft / 12 = ~$6.52/sqft/month
Sqft per effective employee — current: 15,000 employee-used sqft / 50 = 300; future: 10,000 / 30 = 333 (space is actually MORE per person, worth flagging)
math.answer: Annual savings = $740,000. Total future lease = $860,000 (NYC $800k + NJ $60k). Note: new space provides more sqft per effective employee than current (333 vs. 300), so the sizing may be generous.

questions.prompt: Question 3: What costs and benefits do you think there are for Galloway to make this move? Then calculate net two-year savings.
questions.guidance: Candidate should structure a brainstorm covering one-time costs (moving, lease breakage, technology implementation) and ongoing incremental costs/savings (annual technology license). After brainstorming, interviewer provides the actual figures. Candidate then calculates adjusted annual savings, two-year cumulative savings, nets out one-time costs, and identifies that the result is slightly cash negative — failing the CEO's two-year breakeven criterion.

math.setup: Adjusted annual savings = gross annual savings minus annual incremental software cost. Two-year savings = adjusted annual x 2 minus one-time costs.
steps: One-time costs: Technology implementation -$500,000, Lease breakage -$250,000, Moving costs -$250,000; Total one-time = -$1,000,000
math.answer: Net two-year result = -$20,000 (slightly cash negative). This does NOT meet the CEO's two-year cash-neutral breakeven requirement.

questions.prompt: Question 4: We found some data on filmmaking hubs and hybrid/remote work trends. What does this tell you?
questions.guidance: Candidate should read Exhibit 3 and extract strategic implications: (1) post-COVID expectations for days in office have declined across all age groups, especially the 30-40 cohort — adopting hybrid positions Galloway competitively for talent; (2) filmmaking hub bubble map shows geographic concentrations of film production talent, which could inform documentary expansion hiring strategy and whether remote work unlocks access to talent pools outside NYC. Excellent candidates connect these trends directly to Galloway's strategic ambitions (documentary filmmaking expansion) and to the talent market competitiveness argument.

brainstorming.prompt: What costs and benefits do you see for Galloway making this move to a hybrid work model and new office space?

categories.name: One-Time Costs
ideas: Lease breakage penalty (50% of remaining lease value = $250,000)
Physical moving costs ($250,000)
New technology infrastructure implementation ($500,000)
Employee onboarding / change management training
IT setup and network build-out at new location
Furniture and fit-out costs for new space

categories.name: Ongoing Incremental Costs
ideas: Annual software license for remote-work enabling technology ($250,000/year)
Potential increase in IT support costs
Travel reimbursements for employees commuting on in-office days
Offsite server room lease in NJ ($60,000/year — already captured in lease savings calc)

categories.name: Quantitative Benefits
ideas: Annual real estate savings of $740,000 (gross)
Adjusted annual savings of $490,000 after software license
Potential sub-lease income if current space is sub-let before lease expiry

categories.name: Qualitative / Strategic Benefits
ideas: Attract and retain younger talent who prefer flexible work (post-COVID norms per Exhibit 3)
Access to geographically distributed film production talent pools for documentary expansion
Signal of modernity and flexibility as an employer brand
Reduced commute burden may improve employee satisfaction and productivity
CEO proximity advantage (current office near CEO's apartment) is lost — employee and operational consideration

categories.name: Risks / Qualitative Downsides
ideas: New Soho space may not adequately serve employees (higher sqft/person ratio may indicate over-sized or awkward layout)
Employees may dislike moving away from Union Square neighborhood
Loss of in-person collaboration culture for creative production teams
New space lacks server room — dependency on NJ offsite introduces operational risk
Hybrid model may be harder to manage for Production/Post-Production team workflows
CEO's two-year breakeven is too short a horizon for a strategic real estate decision

recommendation: The financial case does not support the move on the CEO's two-year cash-neutral criterion: net two-year result is -$20,000, marginally cash negative

However, there are meaningful qualitative and strategic reasons to consider the move: talent competitiveness in a post-COVID hybrid-preference market, access to geographically distributed film talent pools aligned with documentary expansion, and long-term lease savings beyond year two ($490,000/year net)

Recommend the CEO reconsider the two-year breakeven as too short a horizon for a strategic real estate decision — a three-year view shows ~$1,470,000 in operating savings minus $1,000,000 one-time costs = +$470,000 net positive
If the CEO insists on two-year cash neutrality, the move as currently structured does not qualify and the proposal should be revised or deferred until lease expiry to eliminate the breakage cost
risks: New space provides more sqft per effective employee than current, suggesting it may be over-sized or that space planning was not optimized
No server room in the proposed NYC lease introduces operational dependency on the NJ offsite
Employees may resist the move to Soho from Union Square, affecting morale and retention
Hybrid model coordination costs and collaboration friction for creative teams are unquantified
The CEO's belief that there will be 'significant near-term operational efficiencies' is not supported by the data
next_steps: Validate that 10,000 sqft in the new Soho location truly meets operational needs given the higher sqft-per-employee ratio
Model a 3-5 year NPV to give the CEO a fuller picture beyond the two-year window
Explore whether waiting for natural lease expiry in three years eliminates the $250,000 breakage cost and changes the economics materially
Assess employee and team sentiment on hybrid work and location change before committing
Evaluate NJ server room arrangement for reliability, latency, and operational risk
